GAMP

gamp.Rd

This function computes the GAMP expectation and variance for a given point pattern. GAMP is the nearest-neighbor G analogue of KAMP: it gives the exact mean (and optionally variance) of the uncorrected G function under random relabeling of marks, i.e. the quantities a permutation test would estimate, without running any permutations.

Univariate G is the nearest-neighbor distance distribution of the mark1 points (matches Gest(..., correction = "none")). Bivariate G is the distribution of the distance from each mark1 point to its nearest mark2 point (matches Gcross(..., correction = "none")). Only no edge correction is supported.

Neighbor counts are computed from spatstat.geom::closepairs(), so only pairs within max(rvals) are touched. For variance, this function uses the Rcpp-accelerated implementation.

Usage

gamp(
  df,
  rvals,
  univariate = TRUE,
  mark_var = NULL,
  mark1,
  mark2 = NULL,
  variance = FALSE,
  correction = "none",
  thin = FALSE,
  p_thin = 0.5,
  ...
)

Arguments

df

Either a point pattern object of class ppp from the spatstat package, or a data.frame with x/y columns and a marks column named by mark_var (used to build a ppp internally via a convex-hull window). Should contain one point process at a time.

rvals

A vector of distances at which to compute the GAMP expectation and variance.

univariate

A logical value indicating whether to compute univariate GAMP (default is TRUE).

mark_var

Column name in df containing the marks. Required when df is a data.frame (an error is thrown if it is left as NULL); ignored when df is already a ppp object.

mark1

Variable used to mark the points in the point pattern object for the first type.

mark2

Variable used to mark the points in the point pattern object for the second type (optional, only used if univariate is FALSE).

variance

A logical value indicating whether to compute the variance of GAMP (default is FALSE).

correction

Type of edge correction. Only "none" (no edge correction) is currently supported.

thin

A logical value indicating whether to thin the point pattern before computing GAMP (default is FALSE).

p_thin

Proportion of points to remove when thin = TRUE. Default is 0.5.

...

Additional arguments passed to the underlying functions.

Value

A dataframe with the following columns:

r

The radius at which G was calculated.

g

The observed G value

theo_csr

The theoretical G under CSR, 1 - exp(-lambda * pi * r^2), where lambda is the intensity of the mark1 (univariate) or mark2 (bivariate) points

gamp_csr

The adjusted CSR representing the GAMP expectation.

gamp

The difference between observed G and GAMP CSR

var

If variance = TRUE, variance of G under the GAMP null distribution

pvalue

If variance = TRUE, p-value for G being larger than expected (clustering), calculated using a normal approximation: pnorm(-z).

Details

Computes GAMP expectation and variance

Examples

# one image from the ovarian cancer data in the package
ids <- unique(ovarian_df$sample_id)
img <- ovarian_df[ovarian_df$sample_id == ids[4], ]
r_vals <- c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40)

# univariate with variance
gamp(img, rvals = r_vals, mark_var = "immune", mark1 = "immune", variance = TRUE)
#> We expect the dataframe to be a single point process. If you have multiple point processes, subset the dataframe by ID and please run KAMP separately for each process.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>       r     g theo_csr gamp_csr    gamp       var    pvalue
#>   <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1     0 0        0        0      0      0         1   e+  0
#> 2    10 0.668    0.150    0.150  0.517  0.000219  2.47e-267
#> 3    20 0.869    0.478    0.594  0.275  0.000298  1.65e- 57
#> 4    30 0.920    0.768    0.854  0.0656 0.000120  1.11e-  9
#> 5    40 0.943    0.926    0.954 -0.0108 0.0000391 9.58e-  1

# bivariate
gamp(img, rvals = r_vals, univariate = FALSE, mark_var = "phenotype",
     mark1 = "cytotoxic t cell", mark2 = "helper t cell")
#> We expect the dataframe to be a single point process. If you have multiple point processes, subset the dataframe by ID and please run KAMP separately for each process.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>       r     g theo_csr gamp_csr    gamp
#>   <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     0 0       0        0      0      
#> 2    10 0.392   0.0564   0.0569 0.335  
#> 3    20 0.582   0.207    0.276  0.306  
#> 4    30 0.667   0.407    0.511  0.156  
#> 5    40 0.711   0.605    0.705  0.00543
